rules.statement: When a stored record lacks a member the serving code always writes, treat it as malformed and fail closed: never supply a default, a fallback or another reading for the missing part.
rules.why: Every stored record is one the serving code wrote, so a reader that accepts one lacking what that code writes gives it a meaning the server never gives it. That silently reinterprets a corrupt or foreign record.
rules.check: Look for deserialization or mapping code that substitutes defaults, `?? fallback` values or alternate interpretations when a persisted member is missing, instead of throwing.

rules.statement: Write and read a persisted JSON payload only through the single versioned, replaceable serializer seam (registered with `TryAddSingleton`), never with an ad-hoc `JsonSerializer` round-trip.
rules.why: A bare round-trip cannot handle schema evolution, and a node rewriting a payload drops the members it doesn't know. With one seam, migration stays in one place.
rules.check: Look for direct `JsonSerializer.Serialize`/`Deserialize` calls on stored payload blobs that bypass the payload serializer abstraction.

rules.statement: Store a versioned payload as a self-describing envelope `{ "$ver": N, "$payload": { ... } }` from its first stored document, and have deserialization throw `JsonException` for any document that is not an object with an integer `$ver` and a `$payload`, rather than reading it as version 1.
rules.why: When the envelope is written from the first document, a document without it is corrupt or foreign. Reading it as version 1 would deserialize a document of unknown origin as trusted data.
rules.check: Look for envelope readers that tolerate a missing or non-integer `$ver` or a missing `$payload`, or that treat an unversioned document as version 1.

rules.statement: Declare a persisted payload type's current schema version with its version attribute and have the serializer stamp it on write. Chain upcasters one step at a time (FromVersion to FromVersion + 1), make a missing step throw, and make two upcasters for the same step throw `InvalidOperationException` at construction.
rules.why: Chaining upcasters makes each non-additive change a deliberate, testable step, and fails loudly on gaps or duplicates instead of misreading data.
rules.check: Look for upcasters that skip versions or are not keyed by payload type and from-version, for silently tolerated duplicate registrations, and for a missing step that doesn't throw.

rules.statement: Give a persisted payload type that is updated in place by read-modify-write a `[JsonExtensionData]` member, so that members it doesn't know survive the rewrite.
rules.why: An older node that reads a payload written by a newer node and rewrites it would otherwise drop the members it didn't recognize.
rules.check: Look for payload types written back through an update-in-place path that lack a `[JsonExtensionData]` property.

rules.statement: Before the first stable release, change a persisted payload's shape in place at the current version (add members as required when they are always written, rename, retype or remove them) without a version bump or upcaster. After that release, make only additive changes, or bump the version and add one upcaster.
rules.why: Before release no older stored document must stay readable, so optional members or upcasters for shapes no release wrote carry unreleased state into the first release's code.
rules.check: In a pre-release project, look for version bumps, upcasters, or members made optional/nullable only to tolerate unreleased older shapes, and for always-written members not marked required. After release, look for non-additive changes without a version bump and upcaster.

rules.statement: Let a malformed stored record fail the request that reads it, including list endpoints: a listing must never skip a malformed record.
rules.why: Skipping a malformed record in a listing hides a record the store holds behind a listing that looks complete, while the failure should reach the caller.
rules.check: Look for catch-and-continue or filter-out logic around deserializing stored records in request-path code and listings.

rules.statement: In a background pass that has no caller, log and skip a stored record it cannot process (with the tenant and record identifier) instead of stopping the pass, and never serve or reinterpret that record.
rules.why: Stopping at one malformed record would leave every later record unprocessed, for example sessions and their tokens staying active. A background pass has no caller for the failure to reach.
rules.check: Look for background or hosted-service loops where one record's exception aborts the whole pass, or where a skipped record isn't logged with its identifiers.

rules.statement: Don't ask for a null-check on a payload returned by the persisted payload serializer: it throws a descriptive `JsonException` on a corrupt document or a missing upcaster step instead of returning null.
rules.why: The serializer's contract is to fail with an exception, so a null-check is dead code.
rules.check: Before reporting a missing null-check, confirm the value comes from the persisted payload serializer's `Deserialize`.

rules.statement: Log a protected stored payload that fails to authenticate under the data protector and read it as absent, which is distinct from a malformed payload that authenticates, which fails closed with an exception.
rules.why: The decision gives a protector authentication failure different handling from a malformed record: it is logged and read as absent instead of failing closed.
rules.check: Look for code that throws on unprotect failure, or that silently treats a successfully unprotected but malformed payload as absent.

rules.statement: Require a stored session payload to carry its idle-timeout and absolute-expiry bounds and a session grant to carry an expiration. Fail to deserialize, or throw `InvalidOperationException`, when either is missing, rather than reading the session as ended or unbounded.
rules.why: The server always stamps both bounds when it creates a session, so a session without them describes a session the server never creates.
rules.check: Look for session types whose bound members are optional or nullable, or readers that default or treat missing bounds or expiration as ended.
